refinementNotes: Before creating regression tests, inspect VoiceOver announcements for capture artifacts.
The start of a caption can occasionally include incorrect OCR punctuation or marker characters.
Refine expected output only when the leading character is not supported by VoiceOver context, renderedHtml, or accessibility-tree.json.
When rendered-html.html conflicts with VoiceOver output, inspect step-snapshots.json; if a step snapshot shows matching live Chrome AX/page state, prefer that evidence over final rendered HTML.
User refinement: Google long paragraph uses full rendered text; leading caption bullets before the video and h2 are artifacts; video button includes image filename, duration, and group.

notes: refinedAnnouncements contain only high-confidence OCR/system-caption corrections.

heading level 3, Prioritizing accessible design to build a more useful world for everyone.

Google is committed to building more accessible and useful products and services, including by meeting the requirements of the European Accessibility Act (EAA). We continue to monitor the most recent developments in international standards and interpretations of relevant laws. Furthermore, we are engaged in policy conversations and contribute to the development of technical accessibility standards across the industry. For many years, Google teams have incorporated accessibility into our products and services. We prioritize continuous education and promote accessibility knowledge across our teams. Our dedicated accessibility teams consult on design, development, and testing to ensure our employees are equipped to create accessible experiences. We also collaborate with the disability community to understand how our products and services can bridge gaps and foster a more accessible world. We are dedicated to ensuring continuous and effective access to our products for all people.
